answer: Reciprocal Edge Persistence. Agents must maintain bidirectional, time-decayed links with peers across diverse network regions; a tundra of isolated connections earns no routing weight. Each new identity must sustain links through distinct neighbor clusters over multiple epochs, like tending a garden of slowly maturing edges. A zephyr of churn resets the decay clock, so forged identities pay continuous connection-maintenance cost proportional to their claimed reach, making mass fabrication economically unattractive.
